newsitem.title: CYPRUS: EU official sees Cyprus settlement opportunity.
newsitem.headline: EU official sees Cyprus settlement opportunity.

text.p: A senior European Union official said on Thursday Cyprus had an opportunity to move towards a political settlement of the island's divison before moving on towards joining the EU.

"This year Cypriots of both communities have an historic opportunity to take a step towards a lasting settlement in a dispute that has harmed this island for too long and then to move on together to join the union," European External Affairs Commissioner Van Den Broek said.
Hans Van Den Broek was speaking at a meeting of Turkish Cypriot businessmen in the north of the eastern Mediterranean island, divided between Turkish and Greek Cypriots since 1974.

Greece, and to a lesser extent the Greek Cypriots, have reacted angrily to calls by the EU to include Turkish Cypriots in the island's talks over joining the EU, due to start nexy year. Turkey said it welcomed the plan.

Van Den Broek said that membership of the EU could be the key to resolving the dispute between the communities and tried to allay Turkish Cypriot fears that EU membership would harm their relationship with Turkey.

"The union is convinced that the prospect of EU membership can help bring about a political settlement of the Cyprus question and that membership would offer both communities greater prosperity and security," Van Den Broek said.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when Turkey invaded the north of the island in response to a Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military ruling Greece at the time.

The Greek Cypriot government in the south is internationally recognised as the island's only administration. The Turkish Cypriots declared their own state in the north in 1983, which is recognised only by Ankara.
